title: Selection is rigid over fields and for the known non-abelian cycle-composing laws
subject: Whether the spaces selected by a global failure of a cycle-composing law keep a knot after a line is removed, for fields, blurred laws, S3, D_p and three-value Mal'tsev laws, and the criterion over Z_(p^k)
conclusion: Over a field every global failure of a knot system has corank 1, so removing any line leaves only ties; blurring keeps this, S3 and D_p have only blurred-parity knots on full ranges, and simple non-affine three-value Mal'tsev laws have none. Over Z_(p^k) a failure is global exactly when its class lies in every cyclic subgroup generated by a line's class, and cyclic solution groups leave only ties.
